items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: they remained the Twelve Clouds of Joy, because then they turned the band over to Andy Kirk.

ctx.x: Was a great arranger even then, so we went over -- he set up shop in one of my friend's home, who had a good piano, and everything, named Arthur Alexander, who I mentioned before, that was with us. He played alto and clarinet. And he would call us there and one by one he would have us to come into the room and he would throw a piece of music up and he would play the accompaniment on the piano, and he'd say, 'play this.' He was giving us an aptitude test, in other words. But not like you might do it with kids who…

In other words, we were auditioning. So all of us passed, and we formed this band. Now the band leader was named T. Holder. Now T. Holder was one of the very sharp, good, beautiful trumpet players that had been with Alphonso Trent over the years, and the reason T. Holder was in Dallas is because T. Holder had formed the Twelve Clouds of Joy; Kirk was the bass player, and he had John Williams, Mary Lou Williams first husband in on the saxophone, and in other words, he had formed the Twelve Clouds of Joy, and they…
T. Holder had run away with the money and came back
